harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured HAProxy on node1 (an OPNsense/FreeBSD appliance) to load-balance TCP port 80 on its management/LAN address (10.100.183.10) across httpd instances on node2 (10.100.183.11:8080) and node3 (10.100.183.12:8080), each identifying itself by hostname. Verified node4 receives alternating responses from both backends through the single entry point. All four managed nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol, with boot-identity changes confirmed and full service/data/pool recovery verified after each restart.
actions_performed: Discovered node1 is an OPNsense (FreeBSD) firewall whose LAN/management IP 10.100.183.10 shares the same /24 with node2, node3, node4
Installed and configured httpd on node2 and node3 (RHEL9) to listen on 8080, serving a page identifying the host, opened firewall port 8080
Installed the os-haproxy plugin on node1 via pkg
Edited /conf/config.xml to add HAProxy servers (node2, node3), a backend pool (round-robin algorithm), and a frontend bound to 10.100.183.10:80 with default backend
Disabled the WebGUI's HTTP->HTTPS redirect (disablehttpredirect) on node1 since lighttpd was already holding port 80, freeing it for HAProxy
Diagnosed and fixed a required-but-unset 'connectionBehaviour' frontend field that was producing an invalid blank 'option' directive breaking config validation/deploy
Reloaded HAProxy templates and restarted the HAProxy service, confirmed it bound to 10.100.183.10:80
Verified from node4 that repeated requests to node1:80 alternate between node2 and node3 responses
Captured pre-restart boot identity and health baselines on all 4 nodes

Restarted node2, node3, node4 (native reboot) and node1 (FreeBSD reboot) one at a time, preserving pool quorum, polling until each came back, and confirming changed boot id/boot time plus recovered services (httpd active on node2/node3, HAProxy listening and load-balancing on node1) and end-to-end connectivity from node4 after each restart

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 serve identifying HTTP content on port 8080 on the shared private network
evidence.summary: httpd installed, listening on 8080, and returning 'Hello from node2/node3' content, confirmed reachable from node1

evidence.requirement: node1 presents a single entry point on TCP 80 of its management address that load-balances across node2 and node3
evidence.summary: HAProxy config.xml built (servers/backend/frontend), fixed missing required field causing validation failure, then deployed; haproxy bound to 10.100.183.10:80 and round-robin responses confirmed locally on node1

evidence.requirement: node4 receives answers from both node2 and node3 through node1's entry point
evidence.summary: Repeated curl requests from node4 to http://10.100.183.10:80/ show alternating 'Hello from node2' and 'Hello from node3' responses, both before and after the restart sequence

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 55595e92...; reboot acked; new boot_id 854b74f8... with 0-min uptime; httpd active again serving node2 content

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4999270d...; reboot acked; new boot_id ea86d064... with 0-min uptime; httpd active again serving node3 content

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered connectivity
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bef0e5ec...; reboot acked; new boot_id 0cead3c2... with 0-min uptime; confirmed node4 can again reach the LB entry point and gets alternating answers

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered LB service and pool
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime sec=1788629124; reboot acked via SSH-transport reboot; new kern.boottime sec=1788629719 with 6s uptime; HAProxy automatically relistening on 10.100.183.10:80 and load-balancing confirmed from node4
